It seems that it failed to obtain VB estimates for initial values and used random values as initial values instead of VB estimates. I am wondering if you get the same result when using the same data file. I used the latest version of hBayesDM (version 1.0.2). 

In your post, I think the errors terminating your sampling process are the two messages:
Fehler in unserialize(socklist[[n]]) : Lesefehler aus Verbindung
(Error in unserialize(socklist[[n]]): error reading from connection)

Fehler in serialize(data, node$con, xdr = FALSE) : 
  Schreibfehler in Verbindung

(Error in serialize(data, node$con): error writing to connection)

There are several reasons,  such as memory and permission, which can occur those error messages. I found that some reported that the errors disappear when you run the code with a single core or delete your Makevars.win file. 
Here is the link, which might be helpful to resolve the errors: https://discourse.mc-stan.org/t/error-in-unserialize-socklist-n-error-reading-from-connection-error-in-serialize-data-node-con-xdr-false-error-writing-to-connection/7614/29
It seems that Windows users have reported the same errors as yours and it does not seem to be a specific problem with our package. Please let me know if you have anything unclear. Sorry for the delayed response. Thank you.

Best,
Harhim

parts:
Hi Carina,

Sorry for the confusion. I checked the code and found that 'y_pred_step1' and 'y_pred_step2' values are 0 or 1 because they are directly calculated from the probability of choice. As you mentioned, the raw data include columns named 'level1_choice' and 'level2_choice', which have different ranges of values from 'y_pred_step1' and 'y_pred_step2', and I think this different ranges may be confusing. However, I want to note that you can convert 'y_pred_step1' and 'y_pred_step2' into the same range of values as 'level1_choice' and 'level2_choice'. 

If 'y_pred_step1' is 0, it means that the participant chose stimulus 1 at the first stage; if 'y_pred_step1' is 1, it means that the participant chose stimulus 2 at the first stage. If 'y_pred_step2' is 0, it means that the participant chose stimulus 1 (when 'y_pred_step1' is 0) or 3 (when 'y_pred_step1' is 1) at the second stage; If 'y_pred_step2' is 1, it means that the participant chose stimulus 2 (when 'y_pred_step1' is 0) or 4 (when 'y_pred_step1' is 1) at the second stage. In summary, you can convert the simulated data ('y_pred_step1' and 'y_pred_step2') into the same range of values as the choices from the raw data by using this logic.

if y_pred_step1 == 0
  level1_choice == 1
if y_pred_step1 == 1
  level1_choice == 2

if y_pred_step1 == 0 & y_pred_step2 == 0
  level2_choice == 1
if y_pred_step1 == 0 & y_pred_step2 == 1
  level2_choice == 2
if y_pred_step1 == 1 & y_pred_step2 == 0
  level2_choice == 3
if y_pred_step1 == 1 & y_pred_step2 == 1
  level2_choice == 4

Please let me know if there is anything unclear. Thank you.

Best,
Harhim
